key_concepts: Law of Conservation of Mass states total mass of reactants equals total mass of products
Atoms are rearranged during chemical reactions but are neither created nor destroyed
Balanced chemical equations have equal numbers of each type of atom on both sides
Balancing equations involves writing the unbalanced equation, counting atoms, adding coeff
Coefficients balance atoms in a chemical equation
In a closed system, mass before and after a chemical reaction remains constant
Baking soda and vinegar react to produce carbon dioxide gas, which inflates a balloon
Gas produced in a reaction is accounted for by the mass of the reactants
Relative formula masses can be used to calculate unknown reactant or product masses
If 20 grams of reactants are used up, 20 grams of product should theoretically form
